findings.name: 100% P&T Disabled Veteran Full Property Tax Exemption
findings.description: Effective October 1, 2024, Connecticut fully exempts from property tax either the primary residence owned and occupied by a veteran with a 100% Permanent & Total (P&T) service-connected disability rating, or, if the veteran owns no dwelling, one motor vehicle the veteran owns and keeps in the state (or, if the veteran owns neither, a vehicle belonging to or held in trust for a cohabiting spouse). Separately, veterans with a VA disability rating of at least 10% qualify under CGS § 12-81(20) for an additional exemption on top of the base honorable-discharge/wartime-service exemption, with the additional amount ($5,000 or $10,000) depending on the severity/type of the disability. For assessment years on or after October 1, 2025, claimants for the 100% P&T exemption must annually apply to the town assessor (P&T disability documentation deadline March 31, or an extended deadline per CGS § 12-95) using an application form created by the Office of Policy and Management, including documentation proving the qualifying disability rating.
findings.value: Full property tax exemption on primary residence (or one vehicle if no dwelling owned) for 100% P&T veterans; additional $5,000-$10,000 exemption for veterans 10%+ disabled on top of the base exemption
otherReqs: Honorable Discharge (DD-214) filed with the Town Clerk's office by September 30
Must have served during a period recognized as wartime under CGS § 27-103 for the base exemption
100% P&T exemption: annual application to town assessor with disability documentation by March 31 (or extended deadline)
Additional disability exemption requires filing a VA disability rating of at least 10%
findings.agency: Town Assessor's Office / Connecticut Office of Policy and Management
documentation: VA disability rating documentation (for 10%+ additional exemption or 100% P&T full exemption)
findings.sourceExcerpt: Veterans with service-connected permanent and total disability ratings receive expanded protections. The exemption covers either a primary residence the veteran owns or, alternatively, one motor vehicle... Disabled Veterans are eligible for an exemption in addition to the regular exemption with the filing of a disability rating from the Veterans Administration. This applies to those with ratings of at least 10% under CGS § 12-81(20).

findings.name: Disabled Veteran Registration (Class Code 14)
findings.description: Connecticut waives the registration fee for a Disabled Veteran plate (class code 14) for veterans who submit a letter of approval from the VA on VA letterhead verifying disabled veteran status. The vehicle must be owned or leased by the veteran and registered as a Passenger, Camper, or Combination class. There is no fee for new registration, transfers, or renewals of this plate, though other standard fees (title, lien, Clean Air Act fee, etc.) still apply. A registrant is limited to three sets of disabled veteran plates. Upon the death of the disabled veteran, a surviving spouse may retain the plate for their lifetime at no fee, or until they remarry.
findings.value: No registration/transfer/renewal fee for the plate (standard title/lien/Clean Air Act fees still apply)
otherReqs: Letter of approval from the VA on VA letterhead verifying disabled veteran status
Must own or lease the vehicle; registration class limited to Passenger, Camper, or Combination
Limited to three sets of disabled veteran plates per registrant
Surviving spouse may retain plate for life at no fee, or until remarriage
documentation: Letter of approval from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs on VA letterhead
findings.sourceExcerpt: There is no fee for a new registration, transfers or renewals for disabled veteran license plates in Connecticut under class code 14. However, all other fees apply, such as, title, lien, and clean air act fee, etc. A registrant is limited to only three sets of disabled veteran plates. Upon the death of the disabled veteran, the surviving spouse may retain the plate for their lifetime at no fee, or until they remarry.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran Fishing/Hunting License Discount & Free Limb-Loss License
findings.description: Connecticut residents who are veterans with a VA service-connected disability rating of 10% or more receive sport fishing permits, tags, or stamps at 50% of the regular fee, rounded up to the next dollar (per Connecticut General Statutes governing fisheries and game licensing). Separately, any Connecticut resident (veteran or not) who has permanently lost the use of one or more limbs may be issued a fishing or hunting license free of charge (permits and stamps not included), upon presenting verification of the disability signed by a licensed physician, available at DEEP offices and participating town clerk offices.
findings.value: 50% discount on sport fishing permits/tags/stamps for 10%+ disabled veterans; free fishing/hunting license (permits/stamps not included) for permanent loss of limb use
otherReqs: 50% discount tier requires VA-rated service-connected disability of 10%+ of total disability
Free license (limb-loss tier) requires physician-signed verification of permanent loss of limb use
Permits and stamps not included in the free limb-loss license
findings.agency: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP)
documentation: VA disability rating documentation (for the 50% discount)
Licensed physician verification of permanent limb-loss disability (for the free license)
findings.legalCitation: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 26-27b (fishing permit/tag/stamp disabled veteran discount)
findings.sourceExcerpt: Residents who have loss of one or more limbs or have permanently lost the use of one or more limbs may be issued a fishing or hunting license free-of-charge (permits and stamps not included). Verification of the disability, signed by a licensed physician, must be presented. Connecticut residents who are veterans with a service-connected disability rating by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs amounting to ten per cent or more of total disability shall be charged at fifty per cent of the regular fee for such permit, tag or stamp, rounded to the next highest dollar.

findings.name: State Employment Veterans' Preference Points
findings.description: Connecticut adds preference points to passing scores on competitive state hiring examinations: honorably discharged veterans who served during a recognized time of war (per CGS § 27-103) receive 5 points, while honorably discharged disabled veterans eligible for or receiving VA compensation who served during wartime receive 10 points. The 10-point preference also extends to spouses of disabled veterans unable to work due to their disability, and to surviving spouses of veterans who were eligible for the 10-point preference. Veterans apply for preference points by completing the veteran's preference section of the State of Connecticut Application Form for Examination and Employment (CT-HR-12) and submitting a DD-214 (if not already on file).
findings.value: 5 preference points (wartime veterans) or 10 preference points (disabled veterans, qualifying spouses, and eligible surviving spouses) added to passing state examination scores
otherReqs: Honorable discharge required
Wartime service (per CGS § 27-103) required for veteran-status preference
10-point preference for disabled veterans requires VA compensation eligibility or receipt
DD-214 submission required with application
findings.agency: State of Connecticut Department of Administrative Services
documentation: VA documentation of disability rating/compensation (for 10-point preference)
findings.sourceExcerpt: Veterans receive 5 preference points in state hiring, and those with a service-connected disability receive 10 preference points. Eligible categories include honorably discharged disabled veterans who are eligible for, or receiving compensation for disabilities from the VA and served during a recognized time of war; spouses of disabled veterans who are unable to work due to their disabilities; surviving spouses of veterans who were eligible for the 10 point preference.

findings.name: State Veterans Tuition Waiver (UConn / CSCU System)
findings.description: Connecticut waives tuition for honorably discharged veterans (including Title 10-activated National Guard members) who served at least 90 days of active duty during a statutorily recognized wartime period, are domiciled in Connecticut at the time of admission, and are accepted as matriculated students. At UConn, the waiver covers in-state per-credit tuition for enrolled credits; at the Connecticut State Colleges and Universities (Central, Eastern, Southern, Western) and the 12 Community Colleges, formally admitted veterans receive a 100% tuition waiver for credit courses. The waiver covers tuition only — books, fees, parking, travel, and room and board are excluded. Public Act 18-47 extended eligibility to some veterans with Other Than Honorable discharges (Bad Conduct and Dishonorable discharges remain ineligible). Applicants submit a CT State Veteran Tuition Waiver Application with DD-214 documentation and residency proof, and must recertify each semester.
findings.value: 100% tuition waiver (credit courses) at CSCU institutions; in-state per-credit tuition waiver at UConn
otherReqs: Honorable discharge or release under honorable conditions (Public Act 18-47 extends to some Other Than Honorable discharges; Bad Conduct/Dishonorable excluded)
At least 90 days active duty during a statutorily recognized wartime period
Domiciled in Connecticut at time of admission (including domicile for less than one year)
Formally admitted, matriculated student status required
Covers tuition only, not fees, books, parking, or room and board
findings.agency: Connecticut State Colleges & Universities / University of Connecticut
findings.form: CT State Veteran Tuition Waiver Application; Form D (semester certification)
findings.sourceExcerpt: Honorably discharged or released under honorable conditions from active service in the U.S. Armed Forces (including Title 10-activated National Guard members); accepted and enrolled as a matriculated student at University of Connecticut; domiciled in Connecticut at the time of acceptance for admission, which includes domicile for less than one year; at least 90 days of active duty during qualifying wartime periods.

findings.name: CT Department of Veterans Affairs Residential Facility (Rocky Hill)
findings.description: Connecticut operates a residential veterans facility in Rocky Hill (287 West Street, Rocky Hill, CT 06067) offering a Healthcare Center/Chronic Disease and Nursing Home for veterans requiring skilled nursing care or 24-hour assistance with activities of daily living. Eligibility requires meeting the state's legal definition of "veteran" under CGS § 27-103 (honorably discharged or released under honorable conditions from active service) and being a current Connecticut resident, or having been a resident at the time of enlistment or induction. Applicants must submit an application in advance along with a report of medical history and physical examination and pass an eligibility check; applications may be initiated by the applicant, a service officer, a service organization, or another social service agency directly with the Admitting Office.
findings.value: Skilled nursing / chronic disease care and 24-hour assistance with activities of daily living
otherReqs: Honorably discharged or released under honorable conditions per CGS § 27-103
Current Connecticut resident, or resident at time of enlistment/induction
Medical history and physical examination report required
Must pass eligibility check and demonstrate need for skilled nursing care or 24-hour ADL assistance
documentation: Report of medical history and physical examination
